时事见解
作者: 
司空墨海

item.title: Democrats plunge into a wide-open 2028 presidential race
item.description:
By Tim Reid

WASHINGTON, Nov 5 (Reuters) - With the US midterms over, Democrats are turning to what could become one of their most crowded and unpredictable presidential primaries in decades, a 2028 contest likely to expose the party's divide over how to win back the White House.

No Democrat has emerged as a clear favorite in a field that could attract dozens of contenders, while Republicans ‌have a smaller group of widely discussed candidates, led by Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, to succeed President Donald Trump, who is constitutionally barred from seeking a third term.

Potential Democratic ‌candidates, including sitting governors and senators, have spent months cultivating donors, visiting states with early nominating contests and raising their national profiles, positioning themselves for a race that strategists expect to begin in earnest now that the midterms are over.

The sweeping victories by Democrats on Tuesday, when voters ​delivered a sharp rebuke to Trump and his agenda, will intensify discussions within both parties about how to win over an electorate unhappy with the country's direction.

Despite their resounding victories on Tuesday, Democrats enter the 2028 campaign still divided over whether to tack to the center or move further left on issues ranging from healthcare and taxes to policing and foreign policy.

Republican candidates will face a different challenge – how to distance themselves from Trump after Tuesday's repudiation of his policies. They need to broaden their appeal beyond the president's base while avoiding a break with the populist Make America Great Again movement that has come to define the party.

Trump, who has dominated the political landscape for a decade, may be reluctant to yield center ‌stage, and his continued influence with MAGA followers could complicate the path of ⁠the party's next standard-bearer.

LOOMING DEMOCRATIC BATTLE

Doug Sosnik, a Democratic strategist, said both progressives and moderates will claim vindication in their ideological approaches, ensuring an intense internal battle over the party's future as the 2028 race begins in earnest.

One of the most high-profile progressive wins came in the Michigan Senate contest, where Democrat Abdul El-Sayed easily defeated Republican Mike Rogers in a ⁠likely 2028 presidential swing state, becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.

"All kinds of wings of the Democratic Party can find affirmation in the results last night," Sosnik said on Wednesday. "I don't think that anyone can, nor should they, try to contain the differences we have as a party."

Several potential candidates have either acknowledged considering a White House run or declined to rule one out. Most spent the final weeks of the midterm campaign stumping for fellow Democrats in early nominating states such as Nevada, ​New ​Hampshire and South Carolina.

They include former Vice President Kamala Harris, who lost to Trump in 2024, Governors Gavin Newsom of California and ​Andy Beshear of Kentucky, former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, and US Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of ‌New York, a leading progressive voice.

Reuters contacted representatives for nine of the party's most prominent potential contenders. None confirmed a 2028 run.

Nine days after the November 3 elections, several prospective Democratic candidates, including Buttigieg and another progressive, US Representative Ro Khanna of California, are scheduled to attend a gathering in Denver hosted by Majority Democrats.

The group, backed largely by moderate Democrats and billionaire donor Steve Mandel, advocates for younger party leaders and a party platform that is more centrist.

US Representative Jake Auchincloss of Massachusetts, the group's chair, said the event is meant to spark a debate about the party's future before the 2028 race takes shape, and lay out a positive agenda for what the party is for, rather than just being anti-Trump.

Scott Ferson, a Democratic strategist, said the party's presidential primary could attract a huge number of candidates. "There are at least 30 Democrats who are saying to people close to them, 'Do you think I should run?'" ‌Ferson said.

REPUBLICANS IN TRUMP'S SHADOW

By contrast, Republican 2028 hopefuls have been more guarded, mostly staying in Trump's shadow and deferential to him.

That ​could now change after Tuesday night's rout in which voters expressed deep dissatisfaction with Trump's handling of the economy and foreign policy and ​demanded more action against government corruption.

Vance is in a particularly difficult position, said Matt Dole, a Republican strategist. ​Vance has less freedom than other potential 2028 Republican contenders to put daylight between himself and Trump because he is vice president, a role that traditionally involves defending the president and ‌his policies.

"Vance just doesn't have the wiggle room that somebody else in the cabinet ​has, who can resign," Dole said.

Still, Vance acknowledged on Wednesday ​that the war in Iran, which Trump launched in February and which is deeply unpopular among Americans, had cost Republicans the election. That, however, did not represent a clear break with Trump, who made a similar acknowledgement on Tuesday night.

Whoever emerges within the Republican Party as its new standard-bearer will face the task of keeping Trump's MAGA base onside while rebuilding the broader coalition that powered his 2024 victory. Exit polls ​on Tuesday showed that key constituencies of that coalition, including younger voters, Hispanics and ‌some Black men, had deserted Republicans.

Vance has said there is "a chance" he will not run, citing family considerations, while Rubio has said he has "no plans at this time" to seek the presidency.

Florida Governor ​Ron DeSantis, who unsuccessfully sought the Republican presidential nomination against Trump in 2024, has declined to rule out another White House bid.

Other Republicans viewed as potential candidates include Arkansas Governor Sarah Huckabee ​Sanders and US Senator Ted Cruz of Texas.

(Reporting by Tim Reid in Washington; Editing by Ross Colvin and Howard Goller)

This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/midterms-over-democrats-plunge-wide-111023616.html

item.title: 韩国扩大中东海军部署 但拒绝卷入美伊战争
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

韩国国防部11月5日宣布，计划扩大驻中东清海部队的行动范围，将巡逻区域从亚丁湾延伸至阿曼杜库姆港附近海域，但强调此举不意味着韩国将参与美国对伊朗的战争。

根据部署方案，韩国将增派一架P-8A海上巡逻机、无人扫雷装备及爆炸物处理人员，部队总人数增加约75人，达到395人，并计划将部署期限延长至2027年底。方案仍须获得总统、国务会议及国会批准。

杜库姆港距离霍尔木兹海峡约650公里。韩国国防部表示，现阶段不会直接参与海峡内的护航或扫雷行动。只有在伊朗战争结束或达成停火协议后，才可能考虑参与相关任务，并须另行获得国会批准。

川普此前曾批评韩国拒绝协助美国保障霍尔木兹海峡航运安全。韩国此次扩大军事部署，被视为在回应盟友要求与避免卷入战争之间寻求平衡。

与此同时，伊朗官方媒体11月5日报道，两艘油轮及一艘拖船在霍尔木兹海峡附近发生触雷起火事件，具体损失及人员伤亡情况尚未获得独立证实。

 

关键词: 
韩国

item.title: 分析：美国下一任总统竞争已经开赛，这些是可能的选手
item.description:
未来几周，有意参选的人将开始试探捐款人的态度，走访举行初选的州，并向民调专家和政治策略顾问征求意见，评估自己的胜算。 对民主党而言，目前还没有明确的领跑者。民主党希望这次中期选举取得的惊人胜利，能够让选民淡忘2024年总统选举的惨痛经历。当时，拜登总统直到距离投票日只剩四个月才宣布退选。 共和党总统参选人则面临一个艰难选择：在中期选举遭遇惨败后，究竟应该与特朗普保持距离，还是继续追随他，希望获得他的背书，从而赢得党内提名？

item.title: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assault charges
item.description:
A jury in London has found comedian and actor Russell Brand guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

The actor was charged with seven counts: three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one count of attempted indecent assault.

After the verdict, London's Metropolitan Police Service confirmed that Brand, 51, is facing further allegations of rape from two women, the BBC reported. "The suspect has previously been interviewed under caution in connection with the allegations," the force said in a statement.

Following a four-week trial at Southwark Crown Court, the jury unanimously found Brand guilty on four of the charges. He was acquitted of two rape counts and one count of attempted indecent assault. The judge said he should expect a lengthy prison term.

The claims against Brand were made by six different women, and span from 1999-2009.

Brand had denied the charges and said he had never forced anyone to do something against their will.

Following the verdict, the judge told Brand he would be remanded in custody.

"You've been convicted of a number of offences including rape," Mr Justice Bennathan said. "The consequence of that is inevitably a significant custodial term. My current view is that I therefore have to remand you into custody."

Brand is due to be sentenced at Southwark Crown Court on Monday, 9 Nov.

In a statement, Detective Superintendent Andy Furphy, from London's Metropolitan Police Service, said: "Today's verdict is first and foremost a testament to the extraordinary courage, resilience and determination of the women who came forward and reported what happened to them.

"Despite intense media and public scrutiny, they relived deeply personal and traumatic experiences and placed their trust in us. Without their bravery, this outcome would not have been possible."

The statement added: "Brand used his influence, status and fame to exploit and sexually offend against women.

"As his profile grew, so too did his sense of entitlement. I hope this conviction sends a clear message that no one is above the law, no matter how famous or powerful they may be."

More to follow…

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/article/russell-brand-found-guilty-of-rape-and-sexual-assault-142916771.html

item.title: Mississippi's Senate race is still surprisingly close — and there's no automatic recount
item.description:
Democrats celebrated sweeping successes in the midterm elections as the party regained control of the House, Senate and statehouses across the country.

Democrats flipped seven Senate seats to hold 54 seats to the Republican Party's 44 in one of the most lopsided recent midterm performances. Two seats — nail-biting contests in Alaska and Mississippi — remain undeclared.

Mississippi is unexpectedly competitive, and with 96% of the votes counted, Democrat candidate Scott Colom leads Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by 0.1%, according to the Associated Press.

As Republicans licked their wounds, President Trump signaled he would work with Democrats, but indicated he wouldn't hesitate to use his veto powers. The president also acknowledged Wednesday that the eight-month-long Iran war had hit the Republican vote, but defended his actions. "If I had to do it again, I'd have to do it again," he said, adding, "you can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon."

Vice President JD Vance had earlier blamed the scale of GOP losses on the war with Iran in a post on X, "The real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone," he wrote. "The reason we lost is the war."

Democrats won a series of key battleground contests. In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed defeated Mike Rogers in one of the most closely watched races of the midterms. James Talarico beat Republican Ken Paxton in Texas, becoming the first Democrat to win a U.S. Senate seat in the Lone Star State since 1988. 

Annie Andrews beat Sen. Darline Graham in South Carolina to flip a Senate seat. In Maine, Democrat Troy Jackson defeated incumbent Sen. Susan Collins, putting an end to her three-decade tenure. Sen. Jon Ossoff comfortably won reelection in Georgia. Other Senate seats to flip to the Democratic Party included Roy Cooper in North Carolina, Sherrod Brown in Ohio, Josh Turek in Iowa and Adam Hamilton in Kansas.

As at 5 a.m. ET Thursday, the Democrats held 240 House seats to the GOP's 147, comfortably passing the majority threshold of 218, with 48 still to be called, according to the Associated Press. The latest estimates show that the party is on track to win its largest majority since 2008. And there are still seats it could flip, including Colorado's 4th district, which is held by Republican incumbent Rep. Lauren Boebert, a staunch Trump ally, whose race against Democrat Eileen Laubacher remains tight.

There were also 36 gubernatorial races and numerous ballot measures being voted on. Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms of Georgia became the first Black woman elected governor in U.S. history, while Democrat Amy Acton became the first woman elected governor of Ohio. In Florida, Republican Byron Donalds became the state's first Black governor-elect. El-Sayed will be America's first Muslim senator.

This article originally appeared on Yahoo News at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/live/midterms-2026-live-updates-election-day-voters-head-to-the-polls-as-democrats-look-to-flip-gop-control-of-the-house-and-senate-110000715.html

item.title: 印度金融机构遭AI黑客攻击 部分工具与中国有关
item.description:
来源: 
博谈网

印度计算机应急响应小组（CERT-In）11月4日发布警报，称一个代号为“狡猾猎鹰”（Crafty Falcon）的黑客组织，利用人工智能工具持续攻击印度多家金融机构，包括非银行贷款公司、金融科技企业及加密货币交易平台。

据路透社报道，攻击者使用ARTEX、PentAGI、Cairn和CyberStrikeAI等工具，借助人工智能自动寻找系统漏洞，并以极高速度实施入侵。网络安全研究人员指出，其中至少两款工具与中国有关，但印度官方尚未确认攻击者身份，也未认定事件受到任何国家支持。

美国网络安全公司CrowdStrike表示，中国开发的ARTEX工具此前曾被用于攻击韩国银行，另有与中国有关联的黑客组织利用类似工具，对多个国家的机构开展网络间谍活动。

印度官方指出，攻击者通过入侵金融机构的支付接口，利用受害企业自身的资金拨付系统实施非法转账，并经常选择周末或节假日发动攻击。

今年10月，两家孟买贷款机构遭黑客入侵，损失约200万美元。印度当局尚未证实这些案件与“狡猾猎鹰”组织存在直接关联。

关键词: 
印度
AI
黑客
栏目: 
要闻
